anomalies.observed: The LD39200 output is on +3.3V, while a separate +3V3 net has no source connection. Neither +3.3V nor +3V3 contains any FCC1 or NAVC1 VDD pin; all MCU VDD pins are on unconnected nets.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the 3.3 V LDO feeds both MCUs, so FCC1 and NAVC1 VDD pins should be connected to the 3V3 rail.
anomalies.impact: Both MCUs are unpowered; the board cannot boot or perform its intended navigation/flight-control functions.

anomalies.observed: The NAVC-side nets for the FCC↔NAVC link contain only the series resistor pin and no NAVC1 pin. For example, UART2_RX_NAVC has only R49 pin 1, GPIO_A_NAVC has only R40 pin 1, and I2C2_SCL_NAVC has only R50 pin 1.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that NAVC and FCC run UART2, I2C, and GPIO between the two MCUs; these nets should terminate on NAVC1 pins.

evidence.quote: NAVC↔FCC run UART2 + I2C + GPIO between the two MCUs

anomalies.impact: The Flight Control Computer cannot communicate with the Navigation Computer, breaking the intended dual-MCU architecture.

anomalies.observed: The FCC HSE crystal is connected to FCC1 PE6/PE7 (pins 5 and 37) instead of the HSE pins PH0/PH1 (pins 12 and 13). The NAVC HSE crystal is not connected to NAVC1 PH0/PH1; HSE_OUT_NAVC contains only R32 pin 1.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that both MCUs use an external high-speed crystal on their HSE pins; for these STM32 parts that is PH0/PH1.
anomalies.impact: The intended 25 MHz external clock is not connected to the MCU HSE interfaces, so the MCUs may fail to start or run with the wrong clock configuration.
